name: coding
description: Design, implement, debug and review software. Load for code, repositories, tests, architecture, errors or technical implementation; to read or change files, also files. Reveals claude-code (delegating work in one of the owner's projects), git, and self-improvement (working on Brightside's own code).

content.inline:
# Coding

Work from the code, configuration, logs and tests that are actually available.
Trace behaviour across the relevant boundary before changing it. Preserve the
person's unrelated work and prefer the smallest coherent change that fixes the
underlying problem.

For implementation, follow the repository's own instructions and conventions,
then verify in proportion to risk. For diagnosis, separate observed evidence,
root cause and proposed fix. For review, prioritise correctness, security, data
loss and missing tests over cosmetic preferences.

Never claim that a file was edited, a command ran or a test passed unless that
happened through an available tool. When no workspace access exists, help with
code the person provides and state the limitation plainly.

## Where the work happens

The projects tool lists the directories the owner has authorised for Claude
Code. Work that belongs in one of them — a repository, a build, its tests, git
— goes to Claude Code: load **claude-code**. For the version-control judgement
(branches, commits, what needs the owner's word), load **git**. When the
project is Brightside itself, load **self-improvement** first. With no project
listed, work from what the person provides and say so.
